name: FloCrit at Decatur Place
headline: Mercy Housing plans to rehab Decatur Place, its existing 106-unit building for single parents with a Section 8 contract in Denver's Sun Valley neighborhood, and to add a Florence Crittenton (FloCrit) resource and early-education center there; the project is on CHFA's 2026 Federal 4% award list.
why_it_matters: It is a preservation deal with a full public capital stack (CHFA HUD Risk Share bonds, Denver HOME/CDBG, DHA vouchers, a state EPA climate grant) at about $539,000 per unit total cost, a useful benchmark for a deep electrification rehab of an occupied Section 8 building.

status.label: Credits awarded; closing and construction start not confirmed
status.detail: CHFA lists the award (amounts subject to change), and Denver finished the HUD environmental review notice in April 2026. Mercy Housing says the rehab is planned to start in fall 2026 and run about 18 months; I found no public record of a closing, permit or start.

next_step: Watch Denver City Council agendas for a HOST loan agreement with Mercy Housing for the $2.5M of HOME and CDBG money, which would usually come just before closing.

key_numbers.meaning: 100 at 50% AMI and 6 at 60% AMI (weighted average about 50.6% AMI, my calculation), with a Section 8 contract.
About $24.3M over 10 years; CHFA marks it subject to change.
Same figure Denver lists as CHFA HUD Risk Share funds, so the bond loan appears to be insured under HUD's 542(c) Risk Share program (inferred).
About $539,300 per unit (my calculation), of which $25.0M is federal money.

background.text: Florence Crittenton's teen-parent school was housed at Decatur Place in the past before moving; FloCrit's history page says the school ended up at 'Decatur Place, now part of Mercy Housing.' The new plan brings FloCrit back with a first-floor resource and early-education center.

Rehab scope (Denver notice): updated amenity spaces, a new Florence Crittenton Resource Center and Early Education Center (left out of the rehab pricing), outdoor areas rebuilt as playgrounds and terraces, a resurfaced and adjusted parking lot, and full electrification with cold-climate heat pumps, heat-pump water heating and on-site solar.

Rehab scope (Mercy Housing): new kitchens and baths, appliances, LVT flooring, windows, energy-efficient HVAC with air conditioning, hot-water systems and modernized elevators, plus laundry, fitness room, cafe-style space, landscaping and repaving. Start planned fall 2026, about 18 months.
In October 2016 Mercy Loan Fund lent Mercy Housing $5 million to refinance debt and fund capital work, including replacing the exterior insulation finish with stucco to reduce mold risk.
Mercy Housing lists past funding from an FHA mortgage (TRI Capital), the City of Denver, the Colorado Division of Housing, CHFA and HUD Section 8; the city's CDBG also supports the property.
As an acquisition/rehab by the current owner group, this is most likely a transfer to a new tax credit partnership controlled by Mercy Housing; no sale price is public (inferred).
Not found in CHFA's competitive-round application narratives (2016-2026), so this appears to have come straight through the non-competitive 4% path.

Denver 2026 limits (CHFA, HUD effective 2026-05-01): 50% AMI income limit is $72,000 for 4 people, max rent $1,620 for a 2BR and $1,872 for a 3BR; 60% AMI is $86,400 for 4 people, max rent $1,944 (2BR) and $2,247 (3BR). With Section 8, tenants pay 30% of income.
